items.title: 米軍、オマーン湾で貨物船を航行不能に　対イラン封鎖措置強化へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［カイロ　７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［カイロ　７日　ロイター］ - 米中央軍は７日、対イラン海上封鎖の突破を図った商船を米軍機が攻撃し、航行不能にしたと発表した。

中央軍によると、セントクリストファー・ネビス船籍の貨物船は、イランの港に寄港した後、域内の海域から出ようとした。米軍は乗組員に攻撃対象の区画から退避するよう指示し、その後、米軍機が精密誘導弾で船尾を攻撃した。

米軍は７日、対イラン封鎖措置を強化する措置も発表した。イランが陸上の国境やカスピ海を経由して高性能兵器などの制裁対象物資を運ぶのを阻止するための部隊を立ち上げる。

トランプ米大統領は、イランに新たな攻撃を仕掛ける可能性を示唆している。イラン政府は米軍の基地などがある湾岸諸国に報復攻撃すると警告しており、域内諸国は警戒を強めている。

イラン国営テレビは、ホルムズ海峡にあるケシム島を含む複数の地域で７日夕、爆発音が聞かれたと伝えた。イラン当局者はこれらの地域へのミサイル攻撃を確認しておらず、イラン軍の軍事活動に関連している可能性があるという。タスニム通信は７日、ミサイル２発がケシム島に着弾したと報じたが、被害の可能性に関する公式発表はない。

またイランのイスラム革命防衛隊（ＩＲＧＣ）海軍は８日未明、海峡内の「未承認ルート」を通過しようとした石油タンカー２隻が機雷に接触して炎上していると発表した。ＩＲＧＣが言及した事案が、イラン南部地域で聞かれた爆発音と関連しているかどうかは現時点で不明。

items.title: Gunman Kills Six People in Krakow, Polish Police Say
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: The gunman who killed six people in the historic Old Town district of Poland’s second largest city on Saturday is likely a domestic far-right extremist, according to Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski.
items.body: (Bloomberg) -- The gunman who killed six people in the historic Old Town district of Poland’s second largest city on Saturday is likely a domestic far-right extremist, according to Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski.The alleged perpetrator, a 24-year-old Polish national whose name hasn’t been made public, was injured during an exchange of gunfire with police near the Main Market Square in Krakow and taken to the hospital, where he’s undergoing an operation, Kierwinski said.The suspect drove onto the main Krakow square in a car and opened fire with an automatic rifle at what appeared to be random targets, according to government officials. Those killed included four women and two men, while a further 16 people were injured, the regional police said. Three police officers were injured in the shooting, including one with several wounds in critical condition in a Krakow hospital, Kierwinski said.“Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideology,” Kierwinski told reporters in Krakow. Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Poland was dealing with an act of terrorism.Video taken by a witness and showed by broadcaster TVN24 showed the suspected shooter apparently injured, laying on a sidewalk, dressed in military gear, a bullet proof vest and with a rifle. The defense minister said the suspect had no links to the Polish military.Kierwinski said the suspect had a license for a firearm and that his car was full of ammunition and other guns that probably belong to his family. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said police are looking into “all the circumstances of the attack,” while President President Karol Nawrocki said he’s in contact with the relevant authorities and expects a full explanation of the circumstances. The district in Krakow, a city of some 800,000 located about 250 km (150 miles) south of Warsaw, is a Unesco World Heritage Site known for its medieval architecture. It’s a popular destination for tourists. (Updates with details about the suspect, from the first paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

items.title: ネタニヤフ首相の対抗馬に8日組閣指名、イスラエル　連立交渉が鍵
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［７日　ロイター］ - イスラエルのヘルツォグ大統領は、反ネタニヤフ首相陣営を率いる中道ヤシャル党首のアイゼンコット元軍参謀総長に対し、８日に組閣を要請する。大統領報道官が７日明らかにした。アイゼンコット氏には組閣に向けて最大６週間が与えられる。１０月２７日に実施された総選挙では首相陣営、反首相陣営のいずれも過半数に届かず、連立交渉が鍵になる。

アイゼンコット氏は、国会議員から最も多い６７人の推薦を得ていた。同氏が連携を拒んでいるアラブ系政党も、ネタニヤフ氏や極右政党の政策を人種差別的と見なし、アイゼンコット氏推薦に回った。

アイゼンコット氏はＸに、「今こそ挙国一致の非常事態政府を樹立する時だ。国民の期待に応えられるよう全力を尽くす」と投稿した。

＜連立交渉は厳しく＞

国会総選挙（定数１２０）では、ネタニヤフ氏の右派リクードが単独政党として最多の２７議席を獲得。アイゼンコット氏が率いる「ヤシャル」は２１議席で第２党となった。ただ、ネタニヤフ氏の宗教・民族主義連立陣営全体では５３議席、中道左派から右派までのユダヤ系４政党から成るアイゼンコット氏の陣営は４８議席といずれも過半数の６１議席に届かなかった。こうした中、アラブ系少数派を代表する２政党が過去最多となる１９議席を獲得した。

アイゼンコット政権発足に向けた選択肢は３つ考えられる。一つは、アラブ系政党から閣外協力を得て少数派政権を樹立する、２つ目は、同氏や盟友らが過去に避けてきたユダヤ教超正統派政党と連立を組む、３つ目はネタニヤフ氏と挙国一致政権を樹立することだ。

アナリストらは、３つの選択肢はいずれも実現しそうにないとみている。アイゼンコット氏が合意をまとめられなければ、別の候補者が４週間の期限で組閣に挑み、それも不調となれば議会が別の候補者を指名できる。手続き全体の期限は約１００日で、誰も組閣に成功しなければ再選挙となる。

FAST

EDINBURGH, Nov 7 : Scotland had high hopes of ending their New Zealand hoodoo but again will have to reflect on another defeat after they were within three points of their nemesis at halftime but blown away in the second half of the Nations Championship game on Saturday.
Scotland came close to claiming a first win over the All Blacks last year after fighting back from 17-0 down to level, only to lose out to a late try.
But Saturday’s test offered only flickers of hope for Scottish supporters before yet another dispiriting defeat, extending the All Blacks’ 121-year-old unbeaten streak over Scotland to 34 games.
New Zealand scored 19 unanswered points in the second half to emphasis their superiority.

"I'm clearly disappointed that we didn't put one of our best performances out there," Scotland coach Gregor Townsend said. 
"You obviously prepare to try to win games, but it's more about can we deliver a performance we can be proud of, our supporters can be proud of. And it wasn't there today. So that's frustrating."
It was Scotland’s first game since their three opening matches of the inaugural Nations Championship in July while the All Blacks have had an extensive schedule over the past three months, including an eight-match tour of South Africa and two crunching Bledisloe Cup victories over Australia.
"We were in a good place coming into the game with how the players had trained. But we need more time under pressure and that's what we've got today. This will be a big learning for us," Townsend said.
"We pinpointed a few things before the game that we thought if we could deliver on those, where we would give them some problems," Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu said. 
"And at times we did, but at times they made a mess of our breakdown, so I just didn’t think we delivered to our best standard."

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

items.title: トランプ氏、民主党「脅迫」の調査指示　証拠示さず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ワシントン　７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ワシントン　７日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は７日、民主党が弾劾などの処罰をちらつかせて「多くの人々を脅している」として、司法省に調査を指示した。交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）への投稿で、民主党の行動は「犯罪行為」に当たると主張したが、証拠は示さなかった。

３日の中間選挙では民主党が圧勝し、２０２７年１月から議会の主導権を握ることになった。民主党指導部は、多数派になった後は公聴会を開き、トランプ政権の行動を調査することで、行政府に対する議会の監視機能を取り戻す方針を示している。

トランプ氏は投稿で、民主党が「多くの人々に脅迫状を送っている。全員無実だ」と非難。同党のエリッサ・スロットキン上院議員（ミシガン州選出）にも触れた。

スロットキン氏は１０月のシカゴ大学での講演で、トランプ氏の政策に手を貸した人々を議会が調査すべきだとの考えを示していた。

スロットキン氏は、元中央情報局（ＣＩＡ）分析官で、国家安全保障分野の経歴を持つ民主党議員グループの一員だった。このグループは軍人や情報機関職員に政権の違法な命令に従わないよう呼び掛ける動画を投稿し、司法省が捜査に乗り出したことがあった。結局、大陪審は議員らの起訴請求を退けた。

スロットキン氏は７日、ＳＮＳへの投稿で、この問題は論争になるようなものではないと指摘。「法律を破ったり、税金を使って私腹を肥やしたりすれば、責任を問われるべきだ。法律を破っていなければ、何の問題もない」と述べた。

司法省はコメントの要請に応じていない。

FAST

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Lando Norris put his McLaren on pole position for the third year in a row at the Sao Paulo Formula One Grand Prix on Saturday in tough conditions after a long delay caused by torrential rain at Interlagos.
George Russell qualified second fastest for Mercedes,. 0.204 slower, but dropped down the grid due to a five-place penalty, with his newly-crowned world champion teammate Kimi Antonelli replacing him alongside last year's race winner and champion.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was fourth fastest but has a 10-place grid drop due to power unit changes, which meant Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start third and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg fourth.    
With the rain getting heavier and leaving no chance for anyone to improve on their times in the final phase, the clock ticked down for the last five minutes without a car on track.

"Today is about getting on pole. It doesn’t really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that,” said Norris after a qualifying that started and was then halted for nearly an hour and a half.
RUSSELL ANGRY AFTER ABORTED LAP
Russell was furious not to be fastest, wanting to make a statement despite knowing he had a penalty but having to abort his quick lap when he came up behind Williams' Alex Albon.
"Mate, you told me to back off! What the hell?," he shouted over team radio after realising his day was done. "P2. I don't want to be P2. I want to be P1." 
Isack Hadjar will line up fifth for Red Bull, with Oliver Bearman sixth for Haas. Russell will start seventh and Fernando Alonso judging the conditions to finish eighth as Aston Martin reached the final phase for the first time this season.
Albon qualified ninth and McLaren's Oscar Piastri 10th.
Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen, with a 30 place grid penalty due to power unit changes, sat out the second phase that was red-flagged when Haas debutant Rafael Camara crashed.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who will also be starting at the back of the grid due to engine penalties amounting to an impossible 65 place drop, also went out.
There was then a further delay to clear debris before the decisive third phase.
Conditions had eased in Q2, with double world champion Alonso leaning on his experience and the first to switch to intermediates.
Camara earlier had the home crowd roaring when he reached the second phase but fellow-Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto had a nightmare for the second year running when he went off and qualified last.
Bortoleto slid into the tyre wall with seven minutes to go but returned to the track and made his way back to the pits where the damage proved too extensive to fix in the time available.
Both Alpines also went out at the first hurdle along with the two Cadillacs and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll. 

Source: Reuters

Former youngest champion Fittipaldi hails Antonelli's rise

FAST

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Emerson Fittipaldi said the emergence of increasingly younger title winners was a natural progression of the sport, with drivers now beginning their careers much earlier than previous generations, as he hailed Mercedes' 20-year-old world champion Kimi Antonelli.
Brazilian Fittipaldi became the sport's youngest world champion aged 25 in 1972 and held that record until a then 24-year-old Fernando Alonso eclipsed it in 2005.
After Antonelli's success with Mercedes this season, Fittipaldi no longer ranks among the five youngest title winners, a shift he said reflects how modern athletes begin competing at elite levels from early childhood.
"I think it's great to see the new generation arriving, as in every sport at the international level," the 79-year-old Fittipaldi told Reuters at Interlagos on Saturday ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

"Today, young people start at six, five or four years old."
Antonelli was introduced to go-karting when he was aged five by his father and competed in Formula Two before making his F1 debut last year. He now heads the list of youngest champions ahead of Sebastian Vettel, Lewis Hamilton, Alonso and Max Verstappen.
The Brazilian's own rise was markedly different. Fittipaldi was 17 when he began go-karting and became Formula One world champion eight years later, one of the sport's most meteoric ascents.
For the double champion, who won his titles in 1972 and 1974 for Lotus and McLaren respectively, Antonelli's achievement is evidence not only of changing times but also of exceptional talent.
"He has already shown maturity and performed very well under pressure," he said, pointing to the Italian's victory at his home race at Monza after starting 19th on the grid as proof of his composure.
Antonelli also singled out the race as one of the defining moments of his championship-winning campaign.
"Because after taking the engine penalty, obviously starting from the back, I did not expect such a result. And when I got that, I was like, 'okay, now we just, no matter what, we've got to go and win this'," he told Reuters this week.
MORE RACES IN LATIN AMERICA
Fittipaldi also voiced support for a stronger Formula One presence in Latin America, including efforts to bring Argentina back onto the calendar alongside Brazil and Mexico.
The Brazilian said he would travel to Argentina next week after being invited to inspect renovation works at the Oscar y Juan Galvez circuit in Buenos Aires, which is seeking to return to Formula One after last hosting a race in 1998.
"I think it is very important for Latin America to continue with a strong presence," he said.
"We have the Mexican Grand Prix, which is spectacular, the Brazilian Grand Prix, and we hope Argentina returns. These are three historic races."
On Saturday, Sao Paulo secured its place on the calendar through to 2035, while Argentine officials have intensified lobbying efforts for the return of the race.
Fittipaldi highlighted the region's motorsport legacy, citing Argentina's five-time world champion Juan Manuel Fangio and former title runner-up Carlos Reutemann, Mexico's Grand Prix winner Sergio Pérez, and Brazil's eight world titles, including his own two and three each for Nelson Piquet and Ayrton Senna.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Las debilidades institucionales y de control que expuso la crisis de Ueno Bank en Paraguay
items.author: Juan Pablo Álvarez
items.summary: La calificadora considera que quedaron expuestas falencias persistentes en el control de la corrupción y la efectividad del Gobierno, aunque no prevé un impacto inmediato en el perfil crediticio sober ...
items.body: La crisis desatada por la quiebra de Ueno Bank y sus consecuencias políticas dejaron al descubierto las debilidades institucionales de Paraguay, según advirtió Moody’s. La calificadora señaló que los acontecimientos recientes ponen de relieve problemas persistentes de gobernanza, un historial de controles muy débiles sobre la corrupción y limitaciones en la efectividad gubernamental. En un informe publicado el 6 de noviembre, Moody’s sostuvo que, por el momento, no espera consecuencias inmediatas para el perfil crediticio soberano del país. Esa evaluación se apoya en dos fortalezas macroeconómicas: un crecimiento económico sólido y una deuda pública relativamente baja, que ronda el 38% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB). Sin embargo, la agencia advirtió que la crisis bancaria y la incertidumbre política podrían tener consecuencias más amplias si se prolongan. VER MÁS: Un yate, aviones y carros de lujo: los bienes incautados a Miguel Vázquez, dueño de Ueno Bank en Paraguay El 3 de noviembre, el Banco Central de Paraguay (BCP) anunció que sometía a Ueno Bank a un proceso de resolución, luego de que su índice de solvencia cayera por debajo del 50% del mínimo regulatorio tras ajustes en sus estados financieros. A septiembre, la entidad representaba el 8% de los créditos y el 9% de los depósitos del sistema bancario. Para Moody’s, la quiebra es negativa para el sistema financiero y expone deficiencias de gobernanza y supervisión. No obstante, considera que los riesgos sistémicos permanecerán contenidos si el proceso de resolución se desarrolla de manera rápida y ordenada. La situación también abrió interrogantes sobre la independencia supervisora del BCP. Su presidente, Carlos Carvallo, quien anteriormente había encabezado Financiera Ueno, la entidad predecesora del banco, renunció tras la intervención. Además, legisladores denunciaron un presunto uso indebido de fondos previsionales y posibles encubrimientos institucionales. La calificadora identificó un pasivo contingente para el Estado, aunque consideró que los costos fiscales directos estarían limitados al eventual apoyo de liquidez del BCP al fondo de garantía de depósitos. Según informó el Banco Central, alrededor del 97% de los depositantes estaría completamente cubierto. A septiembre de 2026, el fondo contaba con US$1.600 millones de liquidez, aproximadamente el doble de los depósitos asegurados de Ueno. Moody’s también analizó las consecuencias de la crisis sobre el escenario político, luego de que Santiago Peña anunciara su renuncia el 5 de noviembre, en medio de las protestas y la pérdida de respaldo del oficialismo. El Congreso rechazó su dimisión e inició un juicio político contra el mandatario por sus vínculos personales con el banco. El vicepresidente Pedro Alliana es el sucesor constitucional y se espera que complete el mandato hasta agosto de 2028. Moody’s prevé que mantendría el actual marco de política económica, basado en la disciplina fiscal y la independencia del Banco Central. La agencia espera una transición ordenada que garantice la continuidad de las políticas económicas. Sin embargo, advirtió que una incertidumbre política prolongada o un aumento de la conflictividad social podrían deteriorar la confianza de los inversores y afectar el desempeño económico y fiscal. VER MÁS: Cómo la crisis política en Paraguay puede erosionar la confianza en el país e impactar en dólar y bonos Por último, señaló que seguirá monitoreando las consecuencias de largo plazo de los acontecimientos para determinar si corresponde introducir cambios en su evaluación crediticia de Paraguay.

FAST

Nov 7 : Manchester City's title aspirations suffered a severe setback on Saturday as they slumped to a third straight Premier League defeat, conceding twice in the first half before losing 3-1 to Nottingham Forest to fall six points behind leaders Arsenal. 
City reeled off seven straight wins to start the campaign, but they were beaten 2-1 away by Aston Villa before losing 1-0 at home to Brighton & Hove Albion. 
Champions Arsenal top of the standings on 27 points after 10 games, and City coach Enzo Maresca blamed his side's woes on a lack of intensity as Forest scored their first home goals and secured their first home win of the season. 
"In the first half, when you don't match the intensity, when you lose all the duels, it's difficult, and then when we want to react, it's too late," Maresca told Sky Sports.

"In these kinds of games, first of all, you need to match the intensity. You need to try to win duels - otherwise, it's always complicated. I think (in the) first half we were not good enough in terms of duels. Second balls, we lost all of them, and then when we try to react, we were 2-0 down, and in football, it's always complicated."
DELAP DOUBLE
City gave the ball away cheaply for all three goals that they conceded, with striker Liam Delap, who had only scored once in eight league games this season, netting two sensational strikes to carry his side to victory. 
"It's been coming, and we've been performing like that every week and not putting it in the net. Today we showed we can put them in the net so we're all happy," Delap said. 
"We did everything right, we got the three points and we're going to be happy going into the international break."
Forest coach Oliver Glasner sprinted down the sideline to celebrate Delap's second goal, and he could hardly hide his joy as his side moved up to 16th place on nine points, out of the relegation zone. 
"It was a very good day to play Manchester City but, to be honest, today, the energy in the team and at the City Ground was so incredible that it would have been tough for every team in the world to play against us today," he said.
"All the credit to the players and our fans for this amazing Saturday evening."

Source: Reuters

FAST

CARDIFF, Nov 7 : Wales coach Steve Tandy has admitted there is no hiding from his team’s below-par performance in their 28-21 home Nations Championship victory over Japan on Saturday where they looked flat at times and kept their opponents in the contest.
Wales ran in four tries to collect a bonus point and although it was a third win in five games, Tandy felt his side needed to be more ruthless.
"It's a bonus-point win. It's good to start," Tandy said. "I can't run away from the performance. There are elements we need to improve. I thought we'd be better. We weren't ruthless enough."
Tandy suggested rust may have been to blame as Wales played their first test since July.

"Getting a hit out for the first time since the summer, it does get clunky," he said. "It helps to review after a bonus point win. We'll enjoy it but the beauty of this group is the hunger to get better quicker. We'll definitely have to do that."
Next up for Wales are New Zealand next weekend and Australia. Tandy knows his side cannot afford to offer up cheap opportunities in those games.
"We'd go seven points up and there'd be a sloppy moment," he said. "There was some excitement in what we tried to do. Japan were effective close to the line. We managed the game well outside of that. Defensively, we improved."
Japan coach Eddie Jones felt it was a missed opportunity for his side, who had 62 per cent of the possession but struggled with entries into the Wales 22.
"That could have been a historic win for us," Jones said. "But you've got to be good enough to take advantage of those mistakes. We weren't quite good enough. It was a missed opportunity.
"I'm proud of my team. We had a young team, but they stuck at it. We had a few times where we didn't take chances and Wales did."
Japan face England on November 14.

SANTA CRUZ DE TENERIFE, Spain, Nov 7 : Thousands of mourners gathered at Tenerife's stadium on Saturday to bid farewell to striker Jesus de Miguel, with captain Enric Gallego struggling through tears to honour a teammate who died aged 30 after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision during a match.
De Miguel collided with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono on Monday and was taken to intensive care. Spanish second-division club Tenerife confirmed his death on Tuesday morning.
A huge banner bearing his black-and-white photograph and the words "Forever Demi" hung behind a stage in the centre of the pitch at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.
After a video featuring footage of his Tenerife debut, supporters chanted: "De Miguel, we love you".

Players sat alongside representatives from every club in Spain's top two divisions, including Real Madrid director Emilio Butragueno, as tears flowed in the stands.
"To speak of you in the past tense is tremendously unfair," Gallego said, pausing repeatedly during his speech.
"It's still hard to believe that this has happened to us, Demi; you'll always be one of us."
Demi was the nickname used by De Miguel's friends.
"We're still struggling to come to terms with the fact that you won't be with us again," Gallego added.
Speeches by club directors were followed by a religious service during the 90-minute tribute in Santa Cruz de Tenerife.
Matches across Spain's divisions over the weekend observed a minute's silence in De Miguel's honour.

NEW YORK, Nov 7 : World number one Elena Rybakina has withdrawn from the WTA Finals, the Kazakh said on Saturday, citing concerns over her fitness.
Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk will replace her in the draw, playing Linda Noskova on the opening day on Sunday. 
"I am really sad to inform all my fans and supporters that I unfortunately have to withdraw from the WTA Finals this year,” Rybakina said in a statement. "I’ve had an incredible season but my body is just not physically ready to compete. 
"I’m going to spend some time resting and recovering at home and getting myself ready for the 2027 season."

CAIRO, Nov 7 : Egypt have parted ways with coach Hossam Hassan, with Ali Maher named as his replacement, the Egyptian Football Association (EFA) said on Saturday.
Hassan, 60, renewed his contract until 2030 after leading Egypt to the round of 16 at this year's World Cup, but the EFA said the decision followed a review of recent events.
"The Egyptian FA thanked Hossam Hassan for his efforts during his time in charge and wished him success in the next stage of his career. The board also appointed Ali Maher as head coach of the national team for the coming period," it said in a statement.
Egypt secured their first World Cup win against New Zealand under Hassan before beating Australia on penalties in the round of 32, but squandered a lead to lose 3-2 to Argentina in the last 16.

A 0-0 home draw with Angola in a Nations Cup qualifier in September came under scrutiny, however, after Hassan substituted talisman Mohamed Salah in the 60th minute.
The Trabzonspor forward left the national team camp, with the EFA saying he avoids playing on artificial pitches and would therefore miss the match against South Sudan.
EFA President Hany Abo Rida flew to Turkey this month to meet Salah.
Maher, 52, will take charge of Egypt after a successful spell with Ceramica Cleopatra.
Hassan, who received a three-match ban from FIFA after criticising the referee following Egypt’s defeat by Argentina, left the national team after 38 matches in charge, winning 21, drawing 10 and losing seven.
Egypt face Malawi twice this month in Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Qualifying for Formula One's Sao Paulo Grand Prix was delayed on Saturday after heavy rain swept across Interlagos, the latest weather disruption at a circuit renowned for dramatic wet races and qualifying sessions.
Rain began falling shortly after the end of the third and final practice session and intensified in the minutes before qualifying was due to start at 3 p.m. local time. Drivers initially left the pitlane as scheduled, but a red flag was brought out two minutes later as conditions deteriorated.
As soon as he joined the track, newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli told his Mercedes team over the radio that he was "already aquaplaning". Safety car driver Bernd Maylander carried out assessments of the circuit.
"It's very simple to say it's not drivable, it's too dangerous," Maylander told Sky TV. "A lot of standing water, even on the straights, that creates high-speed aquaplaning."

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON, Nov 7 : US President Donald Trump on Saturday said he had asked mixed martial arts promoter Dana White to serve as White House press secretary and called on him to bring some fighters along as assistants "even though some are not from our country."
White, chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, is a "violent Fighter and Warrior," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.
Trump also asked for six current or former UFC titleholders to join White, including two athletes from Russia's Dagestan region, Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov; Americans Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and "Kayla Harris," likely a reference to Kayla Harrison; and Amanda Nunes, a Brazilian native who became a US citizen last year. 
"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote. White and UFC's parent company, TKO Group Holdings , did not immediately return requests for comment.

The White House press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia's tenure ended last month after less than a week. Zacharia replaced Karoline Leavitt, who left the role at the end of August. 
White and Trump first worked together in the early 2000s, when Trump's Taj Mahal casino hosted some UFC events. But they have become closer allies since the UFC chief publicly backed Trump's presidential campaign in 2016. 
Trump in recent years has attended several UFC events, and in June the White House hosted a night of UFC fights as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence. 
The White House press office already has a former UFC spokesperson in White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung, who worked for White's organization from 2013 to 2016.

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Nov 7 : Arsenal earned a sixth Premier League victory by a single-goal margin as they edged a dogged Hull City 1-0 on Saturday but while his side have opened a healthy lead at the top of the table, Mikel Arteta would prefer a little less jeopardy.
Martin Odegaard's 72nd-minute goal after Noni Madueke's shot had been parried by Hull keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis was enough to break Hull's resistance and secure a ninth win for the champions from their first 10 games.
It was not a comfortable afternoon for Arteta, though, as his side had 21 goal attempts but only converted once.
"To be more efficient," Arteta told reporters when asked what his side need to do to win by healthier margins.

"We are one against one against the keeper. That's happened twice today. There is a penalty there, there is another situation inside the box where the ball is bouncing. So many shots that have been deflected, blocked.
"We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic, he added.
"We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And open, I think, score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game."
Arsenal were not firing on all cylinders on Saturday but will head into the international break in a dominant position after five successive league wins since losing to Brighton & Hove Albion ahead of the first international stoppage.
They are six points clear of stuttering Manchester City and look to be overwhelming favourites for back-to-back titles.
"I think it is time to praise my players. What they have done not only today but after the international break is remarkable because of the games," Arteta said.
"We are not in a really strong position. We know that we can improve in a lot of areas and we'll analyse in this break how we're going to do that. And I will know what to expect afterwards because it's going to be super difficult."

Source: Reuters

Nov 7 : Tesla will add an extra production shift to try to complete outstanding Cybertruck orders before dismantling the line next year for a planned expansion of Cybercab production, CEO Elon Musk said on Saturday.
"The Cybertruck order backlog is currently far more than Tesla can make before dismantling the line for Cybercab expansion around June/July next year," Musk said in a post on X.
"We will add an extra shift to try to get all orders done in time," he added.
The comments come a day after Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory and shift resources toward the Cybercab, a two-seat robotaxi that he has made central to the automaker's autonomous-vehicle ambitions.

The Cybercab is one of Musk's key bets in his push to turn Tesla into an AI and robotics company rather than just an automaker.
The Cybertruck, which began reaching customers in late 2023, has struggled to meet Musk's early expectations. US sales fell to about 20,000 vehicles last year from nearly 39,000 in 2024, according to Kelley Blue Book, far below Musk's initial prediction of 250,000 annual sales.
The stainless steel pickup has also faced repeated recalls and quality concerns since launch, while its unconventional design limited prospects in overseas markets including Europe.

Source: Reuters

items.body: Bloomberg — El ejército de EE. UU. ha anunciado que está creando una unidad especial para ayudar a bloquear las rutas que utiliza Irán para transportar armas avanzadas y otros materiales. El Mando Central de EE. UU. ordenó la creación de la “Task Force Iron Gate”, una unidad compuesta por unos 20 miembros de personal interno, tanto civiles como militares, con sede en Tampa (Florida), según se indicó en un comunicado emitido el sábado. Ver más: Marco Rubio estaría evaluando dejar el Gobierno de Trump tras la derrota republicana en las elecciones El equipo coordinará sus acciones con otras agencias del Gobierno de EE. UU. para impedir el movimiento de sistemas de armamento avanzados, tecnologías de doble uso, materiales sujetos a sanciones y fuentes de ingresos ilegales a través de las fronteras terrestres de Irán y del mar Caspio, según se indicó. “El refuerzo de la colaboración del Centcom con los socios interinstitucionales de EE. UU. limitará aún más la capacidad de Irán para financiar el terrorismo, reconstruir fábricas de armas y reabastecer a sus fuerzas armadas”, declaró el almirante Brad Cooper en el comunicado. Ver más: Trump habla con el emir de Catar sobre los esfuerzos para alcanzar un acuerdo global con Irán Cooper señaló que el bloqueo naval de EE. items.title: Meloni blames pro-Russian hackers for cyberattack on foreign minister
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani, who also serves as foreign minister, said Saturday that hackers had published his personal information on the dark web, citing intimidation as a motive ...
items.body: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for a cyberattack on her foreign minister, after a rise in hybrid disruptions from entities aligned with Vladimir Putin’s government. “The fact that confidential information concerning government officials is being put up for sale is a matter of grave concern and must be addressed with the utmost determination,” Meloni said. Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani, who also serves as foreign minister, said Saturday that hackers had published his personal information on the dark web, citing intimidation as a motive.  “Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted,” he said in a post on X. Tajani has asked for the topic of hybrid wars to be placed at the top of the agenda of a G7 meeting set to take place in Paris on Monday, Ansa reported. Officials close to Tajani said Italy’s cybersecurity apparatus had detected the minister’s personal details in recent days through its monitoring activity, and that they were accompanied by threats and attempts to retrieve more information about him and his family. They said the that because the information was hosted on the dark web, a high degree of anonymity for users accessing it was possible. In screenshots of the dark web pages shared by the officials, similar requests for more information were present for other cybersecurity experts and Italian public officials, including a prosecutor, a police official and a mayor. They are all deemed to be “citizens hostile to the Russian Federation.” The attack on Tajani comes as law enforcement officials report an increase in cyberattacks from hacking groups sympathetic to Russia. Interference has disrupted a range of activities, including mundane operations like funeral homes and supermarket freezers. Meloni’s government is looking into whether outside actors such as Russia had a hand in recent protests that swept Milan and other European cities.  Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov didn’t respond to a request for comment. Italy has been a supporter of Ukraine in its war against Russia since its 2022 invasion.

items.title: La crisis bancaria empuja a un ex presidente a arrebatarle el poder a su protegido
items.author: Ignacio Olivera Doll, Manuela Tobias
items.summary: Para muchos paraguayos, la quiebra del Banco Ueno fue la culminación de una batalla política interna que se había intensificado drásticamente durante los últimos meses entre Peña y Cartes.
items.body: Bloomberg — La crisis bancaria de Paraguay le ha brindado al ex presidente Horacio Cartes la oportunidad de recuperar el poder y la influencia que había cedido a su propio protegido. El magnate del tabaco, que ocupó la presidencia del país entre 2013 y 2018, había sido sancionado por Estados Unidos hasta el año pasado por acusaciones de “corrupción grave”. Un susto de salud en febrero llevó a los paraguayos a creer que los días de gloria de esta figura, antaño influyente, habían llegado a su fin. En mayo, ya estaba listo para enfrentarse de nuevo a sus rivales políticos. “Aunque varios de ustedes querían verme muerto, estoy vivo”, afirmó Cartes, que ahora tiene 70 años. “Van a tener que aguantarme durante mucho tiempo”. Y ahora es su antiguo protegido, el ex presidente Santiago Peña, de 47 años, quien se encuentra bajo arresto domiciliario, mientras que Cartes vuelve a elegir personalmente al próximo presidente de Paraguay. Para muchos paraguayos, la quiebra del Banco Ueno, que esta semana desencadenó la mayor crisis financiera del país en más de dos décadas, fue la culminación de una batalla política interna que se había intensificado drásticamente durante los últimos meses entre Peña y Cartes. Los problemas de Ueno ya eran un secreto a voces desde hacía meses en los círculos financieros paraguayos, tras haber crecido a un ritmo vertiginoso durante el ascenso de Peña a la presidencia y su mandato. El banco —en cuya empresa matriz Peña tenía anteriormente una participación— se benefició de decisiones reguladoras y de una gran afluencia de depósitos procedentes de instituciones del sector público. La crisis se aceleró cuando los senadores alineados con Cartes solicitaron al Banco Central información sobre la entidad crediticia, lo que sometió sus cuentas a un mayor escrutinio hasta que las autoridades reguladoras intervinieron el banco el martes por la mañana. La medida congeló los ahorros de uno de cada tres paraguayos, lo que desencadenó protestas generalizadas. El Congreso —liderado por el líder del partido, Cartes— votó por unanimidad a favor de la destitución de Peña, pero se negó a hacer lo mismo con el vicepresidente Pedro Alliana, de 52 años, dejando clara la elección del “hacedor de reyes”. Alliana fue nombrado presidente el viernes por la tarde. “Sospechaban que el poder de Cartes había comenzado a desvanecerse y que se avecinaba una nueva era en Paraguay. Pero nada de eso estaba ocurriendo”, afirmó Sebastián Acha, un exdiputado que ahora dirige la consultora Pragma. En Asunción, Cartes es tan poderoso que algunos paraguayos ni siquiera pronuncian su nombre cuando tienen algo negativo que decir. En su lugar, se refieren a él por sus iniciales o como “el hombre de la calle España”, la calle en la que se encuentra su mansión, que en la práctica servía como sede de su presidencia. Por eso se convirtió en todo un espectáculo mediático cuando el embajador de EE. UU. en Paraguay celebró una rueda de prensa en Asunción en 2022 para anunciar sanciones contra el hombre que había gobernado el país de 2013 a 2018. A él y a sus hijos se les prohibió la entrada en EE. UU. Washington acusó a Cartes de una amplia trama de corrupción y alegó que utilizó su fortuna para comprar influencia política mediante pagos mensuales de hasta 50 000 dólares a legisladores. También alegaron que Cartes tenía vínculos con miembros de Hezbolá, organización que Estados Unidos designa como organización terrorista extranjera. En 2023, el embajador celebró otra rueda de prensa para anunciar las sanciones del Tesoro. VER MÁS: Así fue como el escándalo de Ueno Bank tumbó a Santiago Peña, aliado de Trump en América Latina Sin embargo, nada de eso tuvo un gran impacto en la política local. Poco después de la primera rueda de prensa, Cartes fue elegido presidente del Partido Colorado, que controla ambas cámaras del Congreso y ha gobernado Paraguay durante décadas. Peña, un economista que ocupó el cargo de ministro de Hacienda de Cartes, asumió la presidencia al año siguiente. La Administración Trump levantó las sanciones financieras en octubre de 2025 sin retractarse de las acusaciones, que Cartes niega. Peña ha negado haber ejercido presión en Washington en nombre de Cartes, aunque en Paraguay se consideró ampliamente que esa medida era algo que él había buscado. Desde entonces, Paraguay se ha convertido en un socio clave de EE. UU. en América Latina, en un momento en que el presidente estadounidense Donald Trump busca ampliar su influencia. Marco Rubio subrayó ese interés en 2024, cuando se convirtió en el primer senador estadounidense en ejercicio en visitar el país en más de cuatro décadas, y la relación ha suscitado mayor atención desde que asumió el cargo de secretario de Estado. Las relaciones, que durante mucho tiempo se han basado en la cooperación en materia de seguridad, se han ampliado al ámbito del comercio y la inversión. Además, es el único país de Sudamérica que reconoce oficialmente a Taiwán, una postura diplomática de larga data que ha dado lugar a una relación tensa con Pekín. “Desde el Gobierno de EE. UU. se percibía —más allá de la propia motivación de Cartes para levantar las sanciones— que mantener las sanciones sobre el político más poderoso del país simplemente no resultaba pragmático a la hora de impulsar el fortalecimiento de las relaciones bilaterales”, afirmó Gregory Ross, asociado sénior de la consultora McLarty Associates, con sede en Washington, y especialista en Paraguay. La política del Partido Colorado también ayuda a explicar este cambio de rumbo. En el momento en que se sancionó a Cartes, una facción rival dentro del partido estaba en el poder. Las sanciones fueron “una medida drástica, pero menos perjudicial para las relaciones entre EE. UU. y Paraguay”, señaló Benjamin Gedan, director del Programa de América Latina del Stimson Center, en Washington. «La situación cambia radicalmente cuando Peña se perfila como el próximo líder de Paraguay, ya que estaba aliado con la facción de Cartes». Mucho antes de llegar a dominar la política paraguaya, Cartes había construido un imperio empresarial que abarcaba los sectores del tabaco, las bebidas, la banca y la agricultura. Su presidencia del equipo de fútbol local Club Libertad también le dio notoriedad a nivel nacional. Cuando entró en política, ya contaba con el dinero, los contactos y el reconocimiento de su nombre necesarios para crear un movimiento propio. Su ascenso fue meteórico. Cartes se afilió al Partido Colorado en 2009, sin haber ocupado nunca un cargo electivo, y creó la facción «Honor Colorado» al año siguiente. El partido le allanó el camino hacia la presidencia al suspender temporalmente una norma que exigía que los candidatos llevaran diez años afiliados. Su intento de mantenerse en el poder terminó en crisis. En 2017, sus aliados impulsaron una reforma constitucional para permitir la reelección presidencial. Las protestas terminaron con el Congreso en llamas y un manifestante fallecido. Cartes abandonó la iniciativa, pero encontró otra forma de conservar el poder: Peña, su antiguo ministro de Hacienda, se convirtió en su heredero político y, finalmente, ganó la presidencia en 2023. Este año, sin embargo, Peña y Alliana, también aliado de Cartes desde hace mucho tiempo, comenzaron a forjar su propia facción dentro del partido. Durante un tiempo, parecieron estar ganando terreno. Gobernadores y legisladores se unieron a ellos y, tras la derrota del candidato de Cartes en las elecciones municipales de Asunción del 4 de octubre, parecía que Cartes había sucumbido. En una declaración del 18 de octubre, afirmó que no presentaría ningún candidato en las primarias del partido. Entonces, Ueno le brindó a Cartes una oportunidad. Los legisladores alineados con Cartes comenzaron a exigir información sobre Ueno, incluidas sus transacciones con partes vinculadas y los depósitos del sector público. Ese escrutinio ayudó a sacar a la luz problemas que, en última instancia, llevaron a los reguladores a someter al banco a un proceso de resolución el martes, lo que desencadenó una crisis financiera y política. Apenas unas horas antes, Alliana había criticado públicamente la gestión de la crisis por parte de Peña, volviendo así a alinearse con Cartes. “Se creía que Cartes se estaba alejando de la política para volver a su imperio empresarial”, afirmó Ross. “Todo eso ha cambiado en la última semana”. Cartes respaldó entonces los esfuerzos para destituir a su antiguo protegido. Peña perdió rápidamente el apoyo de su partido, mientras que Alliana sobrevivió a un intento de destitución y se erigió como su sucesora. VER MÁS: Caída de Ueno Bank golpea a la economía informal de Paraguay por la lentitud en las devoluciones “Se trata, en parte, de una lucha por el liderazgo político”, afirmó Dionisio Borda, exministro de Hacienda que asesoró a Peña cuando este ocupaba el cargo de ministro bajo el mandato de Cartes. “Cartes ejerce una enorme influencia sobre la política paraguaya debido a su gran poderío económico y a su fuerte ansia de poder. En gran medida, sigue ostentando el poder político en Paraguay”, Borda, sin embargo, atribuye la responsabilidad del colapso de Ueno a Peña, calificándolo de “fraude contra sus clientes” y señalando el crecimiento exponencial del banco impulsado por fondos públicos, incluidos unos 850 millones de dólares procedentes del Gobierno y del fondo de pensiones estatal IPS. “Siempre consideré a Peña una persona ambiciosa, pero nunca imaginé que sus ambiciones financieras y monetarias llegarían tan lejos”, afirmó Borda. Lea más en Bloomberg.com VER MÁS: Lula hará un ajuste fiscal en Brasil pese al escepticismo del mercado, dice Oxford Economics

Nov 7 : Binance's finance chief Kaiser Ng is leaving the company to pursue another venture, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange said days after hackers stole $6.3 billion from the platform in a record heist.
"Kaiser Ng has decided to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance, with a transition plan implemented over the last half year," Binance Co-Chief Executive Officer Yi He said in a statement on Saturday.
Justin Yek, a longtime finance executive who was most recently vice-president of finance at Airwallex, is taking over as CFO.
The announcement comes just over a week after Binance said hackers stole cryptocurrency in a sophisticated attack that began months earlier with the compromise of several employees' computers.

Binance has said the breach, which unfolded on October 29, started with malware hidden in software downloads and fake job recruitment efforts targeting engineers. It said it will fully reimburse affected customers.
The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group for the theft, an allegation Pyongyang has denied.
Ng has been CFO at Binance since January 2022 and has previously worked at rival crypto exchange Kraken, according to his LinkedIn profile.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[７日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は、一時管理下に置く日本たばこ産業（ＪＴ）傘下のロシア資産を拡大、新たに３社を対象に加えた。

プーチン氏は５日、ＪＴの海外子会社、ＪＴインターナショナル（ＪＴＩ）のロシア資産を一時管理下に置く大統領令に署名、ＪＴＩがロシアに保有する４社がインダストリアル・アセッツの管理下に置かれた。

夜間に公表された今回の大統領令では、対象を３社追加。いずれもＪＴＩインベストメンツが保有する企業で、インタファクス通信によると、３社は輸入、経営管理、持ち株会社としての機能を担っている。

一方、ロシアのメディアＲＢＣは７日、インダストリアル・アセッツのアントン・ピボバロフ代表が、生産と既存の人員体制を維持し、従業員や取引先に対する義務を滞りなく履行することを目指すと述べたと報じた。

大統領令は今回の措置の理由を示していない。ロシア大統領府はこれまで、同様の資産接収について、ロシアに敵対的と見なす国々の行動に対応したものだと説明している。

ロシア事業はＪＴグループの売上高の約１０％、営業利益の約２５％を占める。

ＪＴのロゴ、東京の本社で10月13日撮影 REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon/File Photo（ロイター） [７日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は、一時管理下に置く日本たばこ産業（ＪＴ）傘下のロシア資産を拡大、新たに３社を対象に加えた。

プーチン氏は５日、ＪＴの海外子会社、ＪＴインターナショナル（ＪＴＩ）のロシア資産を一時管理下に置く大統領令に署名、ＪＴＩがロシアに保有する４社がインダストリアル・アセッツの管理下に置かれた。

夜間に公表された今回の大統領令では、対象を３社追加。いずれもＪＴＩインベストメンツが保有する企業で、インタファクス通信によると、３社は輸入、経営管理、持ち株会社としての機能を担っている。

一方、ロシアのメディアＲＢＣは７日、インダストリアル・アセッツのアントン・ピボバロフ代表が、生産と既存の人員体制を維持し、従業員や取引先に対する義務を滞りなく履行することを目指すと述べたと報じた。

大統領令は今回の措置の理由を示していない。ロシア大統領府はこれまで、同様の資産接収について、ロシアに敵対的と見なす国々の行動に対応したものだと説明している。

ロシア事業はＪＴグループの売上高の約１０％、営業利益の約２５％を占める。

Finland plans anti-tank barriers on Russian border as Moscow rearms

Finland is reviewing Ukraine-style defences and strengthening its military, which can mobilise 280,000 troops in wartime, to deter a Russian attack.

Kirsi Heikel

07 November, 2026 09:36 pm IST

Follow Us:

Finland is studying Ukraine-style anti-tank obstacles to bolster its border with Russia as it works to strengthen defenses on NATO’s eastern flank against a rapidly rearming foe.

Lieutenant General Pasi Välimäki, commander of the Finnish Army, said in an interview that Russia had already begun rebuilding its military capacity, even as its full-scale invasion of Ukraine grinds into a fifth year.

In that conflict, Kyiv’s forces have used extensive defensive lines and anti-tank obstacles to slow attackers. Neither side has found a reliable way to break through them and restore large-scale movement and maneuver, Välimäki said.

Show Full Article

Sharing a 1,340-kilometer (830-mile) border with Russia, accounting for about half of NATO’s land frontier with that country, Finland must determine how structures similar to those used in Ukraine would fare in harsh northern weather.

“Conditions in Finland are more challenging,” Välimäki said. “If we build fortifications and dig anti-tank ditches or obstacles as deep as those in Ukraine, how long does it take before our environment turns them into artificial ponds?”

Russia’s efforts to replenish its weapons stockpiles are starting to show some effects, he said, with T-90 tanks, BMP-3 infantry fighting vehicles and 2S19 self-propelled howitzers being delivered to storage sites.

Finland lacks the capacity to prevent that rearming. Rather, the goal is to deter Russia by convincing its military that an attack would fail, he said.

“Everything we are doing now is about creating a threshold so that Russia does not go any further, whether we are talking about the alliance or Finland,” Välimäki said.

Finland continued conscription and maintained territorial defense reserves after the Cold War, even as many European nations reduced their forces. Despite a population of just 5.6 million, its military can call on about 280,000 troops in wartime.

“When the war in Ukraine began, we improved our readiness and put 60,000 people through refresher training over two years,” Välimäki said. “We also quickly began replenishing stocks of critical materiel.”

Finland is now carrying out an overhaul of its land forces that will run through the end of the 2030s, covering equipment, force structure, readiness and the capacity to sustain combat. The basic approach — deterring an attack by being prepared — hasn’t changed, Välimäki said. What has changed is the scale required.

“The scale of the ammunition, production systems and trained personnel that we need to have ready for use is different from what it was before 2022,” he said. “It has to be larger, more sustainable and technologically more advanced than before.”

Finland will spend at least as much on the overhaul of its land forces as on its ongoing strategic Navy and Air Force programs combined, the Defense Ministry said in a written statement. Those programs have total funding of €11.6 billion ($13 billion).

As part of a much broader procurement drive, Finland is expanding its Hanwha Aerospace Co. Ltd. K9 self-propelled howitzer fleet, modernizing its heavy multiple-launch rocket systems to fire almost 500 kilometers, and preparing to replace its BMP-2 infantry fighting vehicles.

Attacks on Ukraine have shown the scale of the air and missile threat Finland may face. Under the alliance’s Eastern Flank Deterrence Line concept, it isn’t enough to shoot down incoming missiles and drones — defenders must also be able to strike the launchers before they fire, Välimäki said.

“For Finns, this is a difficult issue, because it means hitting targets on the Russian side,” he said.

Finland has already begun replacing its F/A-18 Hornets with 64 Lockheed Martin Corp. F-35A fighters, with the first aircraft delivered. It has also ordered Israel’s David’s Sling missile-defense system, produced by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems Ltd., which has seen extensive action in the Iran war.

Välimäki rejects the idea that new technology has made traditional weapons obsolete. Drones have become a major part of the battlefield, Välimäki said, adding that they are only one element to consider.

Ukraine has also underscored the need to replenish equipment and ammunition during a prolonged conflict, and Välimäki wants domestic production that can expand rapidly.

“What I would like Finland to have is the ability to scale for mass-production in large volumes — production for readiness and daily training consumption that can be maintained in peacetime and scaled up tenfold in crisis and conflict,” he said.

The push reflects a fundamental constraint on how Finland can fight a much larger opponent on the eastern flank of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

“We do not want a war of attrition,” Välimäki said. “We are a country of five million people, and we cannot operate on that logic.”

Cyberattack at Russian stats agency Rosstat delays major economic reports

Rosstat failed to publish two scheduled weekly price releases as scheduled Friday, postponing them repeatedly before finally issuing the data. Some previously published information is also absent from the Rosstat website.

Bloomberg News

07 November, 2026 09:31 pm IST

Follow Us:

Representational image | Photo: Flickr

Stay updated with ThePrint:

Major Russian economic reports will be delayed through at least Nov. 13 following a recent major hack on the statistics agency Rosstat.

Rosstat failed to publish two scheduled weekly price releases as scheduled on Friday, postponing them repeatedly before finally issuing the data. Some previously published information is also absent from the Rosstat website.

The agency said it’s continuing to restore systems after a cyberattack knocked parts of its infrastructure offline, without providing more detail.

Show Full Article

“To ensure data security, some parts of the infrastructure remain isolated. This is necessary to allow thorough checks and a phased restoration of access,” the agency said on Thursday. “As a result, some website functions and parts of the IT infrastructure may be temporarily unavailable.”

While its website has resumed operating, deadlines for companies to submit statistical reports have been extended through Nov. 13. The longer collection period may result in further delays to individual data releases, the agency said.

The Belarusian pro-opposition group Cyber Partisans and the hacker operation Silent Crow claimed on Nov. 1 that they’d breached Rosstat’s internal infrastructure, gaining access to about 25,000 computers and extracting some 23 terabytes of data, including information on Russian military losses in the war against Ukraine.

Rosstat said that targeted cyberattacks on its systems were detected between Oct. 29 and Nov. 1, but that it found no evidence its databases had been compromised or confidential information leaked.

Since President Vladimir Putin invaded Ukraine in 2022, the Kremlin has steadily restricted public access to official data, withholding or classifying an expanding range of information, including many economic and demographic indicators.

items.title: Lula hará un ajuste fiscal en Brasil pese al escepticismo del mercado, dice Oxford Economics
items.author: Juan Pablo Álvarez
items.summary: El presidente reelecto pertenece al espectro político de la centroizquierda, pero muy posiblemente deba recurrir a la austeridad.
items.body: El presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, llevará adelante un ajuste fiscal durante su último mandato, pese al escepticismo de los mercados sobre su compromiso con la consolidación de las cuentas públicas. Así lo proyecta Oxford Economics, que, de todos modos, anticipa que el proceso será gradual y podría decepcionar a los inversores tanto por su velocidad como por su magnitud. En un informe publicado el 5 de noviembre, el economista sénior de la consultora británica, Mauricio Monge, sostiene que los mercados brasileños adoptaron una postura excesivamente pesimista sobre la capacidad del Gobierno para controlar la deuda pública. A su juicio, la reciente venta de activos brasileños significó una corrección exagerada después del repunte que había provocado el resultado de la primera vuelta electoral del ex candidato Flávio Bolsonaro. La posibilidad de revertir de manera sostenida esa tendencia dependerá, según el análisis, de que Lula consiga demostrar que puede encaminar las cuentas públicas mediante un ajuste fiscal creíble y sostenible. VER MÁS: Nubank suspende depósitos y retiros de criptomonedas en Brasil por problema de un proveedor externo El proyecto de presupuesto brasileño para 2027 contempla una consolidación fiscal gradual durante los próximos años. El Gobierno apunta a alcanzar un superávit primario del 0,5% del PBI en el sector público no financiero, mientras que Oxford Economics proyecta un déficit del 0,2%. Aunque tanto la administración brasileña como la consultora esperan que el país consiga superávits primarios en los próximos años, esos resultados quedarían por debajo del nivel necesario para estabilizar la deuda pública, estimado en un superávit cercano al 2% del PBI. La principal vía para mejorar el resultado fiscal sería desacelerar el crecimiento real del gasto primario bajo las reglas fiscales vigentes. Oxford Economics estima que las erogaciones primarias aumentarán un promedio del 1,5% anual en términos reales entre 2027 y 2030, frente al 4,2% registrado entre 2022 y 2026. Los ingresos, por su parte, crecerían un 3% anual durante ese período. Sin embargo, la composición del presupuesto limita las posibilidades de un recorte más profundo. Más del 90% del gasto primario es obligatorio y está indexado al salario mínimo, la inflación o los ingresos del Gobierno. Además, la consultora considera improbable que Lula avance sobre el gasto social. Las prestaciones previsionales y los programas de protección social representan una porción importante de las erogaciones. Para 2027, el presupuesto contempla un aumento promedio del 12,4% en estos gastos. Oxford Economics señala que Lula parece reconocer las preocupaciones fiscales del mercado. En esa dirección, el ministro de Hacienda, Dario Durigan, anticipó que el Gobierno presentará modificaciones al proyecto de presupuesto de 2027 para congelar partidas de gasto. No obstante, la consultora espera que el impacto de esas medidas sea limitado por el peso de las erogaciones obligatorias. Por eso, aguardará la aprobación del Congreso antes de modificar sus proyecciones. El escenario también contempla riesgos de que Lula impulse nuevas medidas populistas durante su último mandato. Sin embargo, Oxford Economics considera que su margen de acción estará restringido por un Congreso que se desplazó todavía más hacia la derecha. VER MÁS : Lula deberá buscar alternativas para fortalecer el capital de Banco do Brasil ante la presión crediticia El informe concluye que el principal desafío del presidente será convencer a los mercados de que puede implementar un ajuste fiscal sostenible, una condición que considera central para recuperar la confianza de los inversores.

Nov 7 : Russian President Vladimir Putin has expanded the list of Japan Tobacco International (JTI) businesses placed under temporary administration in Russia, adding three more companies to those included in the original order issued on Thursday.
On Thursday, Putin signed a decree transferring the Russian assets of JTI, part of Japan Tobacco Inc. and Russia's largest tobacco manufacturer, to temporary management, making the tobacco group the latest foreign company to lose control of local operations as Moscow tightens its grip on overseas-owned assets.
According to the original decree, the stakes in four JTI businesses were placed under the administration of Russian company Industrial Assets.
A separate decree, published overnight, extended the measure to three additional companies, all owned by JTI Investments Sarl According to Interfax news agency, the three firms acted as import, management and holding companies.

Separately, Russian media outlet RBC on Saturday quoted Anton Pivovarov, head of Industrial Assets, as saying the company would seek to maintain production, preserve existing teams and fulfil obligations to employees and business partners without disruption.
Putin's decrees gave no reason for the move, but the Kremlin has previously linked similar asset seizures to actions taken by countries it considers hostile to Russia.
In an emailed statement issued after the first decree, JTI said it was aware of the decision and was "assessing the situation and our options, prioritising our stakeholders, most notably our employees".
The Japanese government owns around 37 per cent of shares in Japan Tobacco Inc., whose brands include Winston and Camel cigarettes.
The Russian business accounts for about 10 per cent of Japan Tobacco Group's revenue and roughly 25 per cent of its operating profit.

New Zealand election first count ends with two main parties nearly deadlocked

By Lucy Craymer and Alasdair Pal
WELLINGTON, Nov 7 (Reuters) – New Zealand’s ruling centre-right National Party and main opposition Labour were nearly deadlocked in the popular vote after initial counting in the nationwide general election on Saturday.

Results from the Electoral Commission show that with more than 95% of the ballots counted, both parties were polling just short of 30% of the popular vote, with just a few thousand votes separating the two.

A projection from New Zealand’s Electoral Commission showed the current three-party ruling coalition led by National would have a majority of two seats, after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter disillusionment with the two biggest contenders.

Show Full Article

Both parties said it would take time for the final results to be known.

“It is heartening to see that on the numbers so far, National is once again the largest party in parliament, and we have a pathway to forming the next government,” Prime Minister Christopher Luxon told supporters in Auckland.

“But I have to tell you right now, it is too close to call.”

Labour leader Chris Hipkins delivered a similar message in Upper Hutt, a city northeast of the capital Wellington.

“Tonight, New Zealand has spoken. It may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you’ve said,” he told supporters.

GOVERNMENT COULD TAKE WEEKS

Special votes, which include those from overseas voters or people outside their electorate, will not be included in the vote count until official results are released on November 27.

Those votes have typically favoured the left, with parties on the right losing support following the count. This could also be key in seats where races remain tight between Labour and National candidates.

Left-leaning parties including Labour are aiming to make the National-led coalition the first one-term government in just over 50 years.

New Zealand’s electoral system makes coalitions the norm, and the tightness of this year’s race means one or more of the country’s smaller parties will almost certainly participate in a governing coalition.

The country switched to a mixed member proportional system in 1996, which means people vote for both the party and a local constituency candidate.

There are 71 constituency seats and at least 49 party seats, and a party or coalition needs a majority to form a government.

MINOR PARTIES WILL BE KEY

Popular support for Labour and National is at historically low levels, with surveys showing voters have lost faith in the major parties to find solutions to the sluggish economy and to make the necessary changes to fix ageing infrastructure.

If the National-led coalition loses its majority at the official count, either it or a left-leaning coalition would require the support of the centrist Opportunity Party, which looks likely to enter parliament for the first time.

Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong said she would look to negotiate with the party that secured the largest number of seats after the official results.

“We made that call based on the fact that we need a majority of seats in parliament in order to form a government. So that is what we will stick to,” she told public broadcaster TVNZ.

New Zealand has emerged only slowly from a prolonged economic downturn, with growth subdued, household budgets strained and unemployment rising to 5.7% in the third quarter, its highest level in 11 years.

Healthcare and hospitals rank alongside the economy as leading concerns for voters, while housing affordability is still a major issue, even though house prices have broadly stabilised.

Indigenous Maori voters are also concerned about the current government’s attempts to roll back historic policies meant to improve conditions for the community as well as efforts to reduce the influence of the country’s founding document, the Treaty of Waitangi, on policy.

(Reporting by Alasdair Pal and Lucy Craymer in Wellington; Editing by Saad Sayeed and Hugh Lawson)

Astronomers spot white dwarf star with two rings of planetary debris

Artist's impression shows two gaseous discs of debris from planetary wreckage around the white dwarf J1328−1450 –– the dead core of a star similar to our sun that expelled its outer layers at the end of its lifetime. The star was suspected to have had a planetary system that was vaporized to rubble as the star died, and this debris ended up arranged in a disc arrangement like the one shown here, in this handout image released by the European Southern Observatory on October 27, 2026. FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 7 : Billions of years from now, the sun is expected to run out of fuel and greatly expand into what is called a red giant, eventually shedding its outer layers and leaving behind its dense core, a white dwarf. Some of the planets in our solar system would be destroyed while others might survive.
Researchers have now spotted a white dwarf with planetary debris swirling around it in an unusual configuration that may offer a peek into one possible outcome for our solar system in the distant future.
Unlike in similar systems previously observed, the debris disc surrounding this white dwarf appears to consist of two distinct rings. The researchers said the disc may have been shaped by two planetary or smaller rocky bodies that are embedded in the rings after managing to survive the star's violent death throes.
The white dwarf, named J1328−1450, is located in the Milky Way roughly 1,600 light-years from Earth, in the constellation Virgo. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km). The observations were made using the European Southern Observatory's Chile-based Very Large Telescope.

Prior to this discovery, astronomers had identified 21 white dwarfs with debris surrounding them, all of which had a single disc and not a double ring of material as the new observations reveal.
"It shows that the remnants of a planetary system can have a much more complex structure than we previously thought, and provides further support to the idea that planetary rocky bodies may survive the transformation of a star into a white dwarf," said astronomer Felipe Lagos-Vilches of Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María in Chile, one of the authors of the study published in the journal Nature Astronomy.
The white dwarf has a mass about 47 per cent that of the sun, jam-packed into a diameter roughly the same as that of Earth.
The surviving planetary bodies may be remnants of larger and heavily disrupted planets. One of them may be around the size of the dwarf planet Pluto, with the other one smaller than that.
Lagos-Vilches said the original star may have hosted a planetary system before it expanded dramatically into a red giant, engulfing some of the innermost planets while ones with more distant orbits survived.
"The planetary system did not completely disappear. Some surviving rocky bodies may have been gravitationally perturbed onto highly eccentric orbits that brought them close to the white dwarf," Lagos-Vilches said.
"Objects that came sufficiently close were disrupted by the white dwarf's gravitational force. Their material was spread into a debris disc containing dust and gas. However, two relatively large rocky bodies may have survived within this debris," Lagos-Vilches said. 
The presence of the two bodies may help explain the distribution of the surrounding material into a pair of concentric gaseous rings, Lagos-Vilches said. 
"The outer ring is strongly depleted in magnesium compared with the inner ring. This suggests that they may originate from different parent bodies, or possibly from different layers of a rocky body that was disrupted when it went too close to the white dwarf due to its strong gravitational field," Lagos-Vilches said.
A GLIMPSE OF THE FUTURE
In about 5 billion years, the sun will become a red giant, Lagos-Vilches said.
"It will eventually lose its outer layers and become a white dwarf. The inner solar system will be dramatically affected. Mercury and Venus are expected to be engulfed by the expanding sun, while there is still no clear consensus on whether Earth will also be engulfed during this phase. The fate of the outer planets is different. Jupiter, Saturn and the more distant bodies should have a much better chance of surviving," Lagos-Vilches said.
After the sun becomes a white dwarf, surviving planetary remnants, moons and asteroids could potentially be drawn close enough to the white dwarf to be torn apart by gravitational forces.
"A debris disc like the one around J1328−1450 could therefore represent one possible stage in the very distant future of our own planetary system," Lagos-Vilches said.

Source: Reuters

items.summary: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported.
items.body:
US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed launches 'Habibi PAC' days after historic election win Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported.
ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 21:32 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 21:32 IST

Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported. According to Al Jazeera, citing a filing submitted to the Federal Election Commission (FEC) on Thursday, Habibi PAC has been registered as a leadership PAC sponsored by El-Sayed. Such committees operate separately from a politician's own election campaign and are used to raise and spend funds in support of other political candidates and political activities.
The name 'Habibi', an Arabic term of endearment meaning 'my dear' or 'my beloved', is a phrase El-Sayed frequently used during his election campaign. He also used the expression while addressing US Vice President JD Vance during his victory speech in Detroit, saying, "JD, habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January."
El-Sayed is among several newly elected Democratic lawmakers who have registered leadership PACs following Tuesday's election, according to FEC filings. Others include Arizona Congressman-elect Amish Shah, who registered 'PACStreet Boy', Iowa Senator-elect Josh Turek, who launched 'WheelPAC', and North Carolina Senator-elect Roy Cooper, who registered 'One NC PAC', as reported by Al Jazeera.
According to Al Jazeera, citing OpenSecrets, leadership PACs are often used by ambitious lawmakers to build influence among their colleagues and strengthen their prospects of securing party leadership positions or committee chairmanships. They typically contribute to other lawmakers, political parties and political committees.
During the 2024 election cycle, leadership PACs contributed USD 79.3 million to federal candidates. While most of the contributions went to Republican candidates, a Democratic leadership PAC emerged as the largest individual donor, Al Jazeera reported, citing OpenSecrets. El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, defeated Republican candidate Mike Rogers following a campaign in which US President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Senator Ted Cruz questioned his loyalty, called him a "jihadist" and attempted to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood movement without providing evidence.
Getting money out of politics was among El-Sayed's central campaign pledges. During his victory speech, he highlighted the significance of his electoral success, saying that in a contest between money and the people, "the many can win". His victory came amid the most expensive midterm election on record.
According to Al Jazeera, an analysis of FEC data by OpenSecrets noted that total spending in the election cycle is expected to reach USD 11.9 billion, compared with USD 8.9 billion in 2022. Outside spending, largely driven by super PACs, is projected to reach USD 3.9 billion, marking an 85 per cent increase from the 2022 midterm elections.
Meanwhile, so-called dark money contributions from donors whose identities are not disclosed have already reached at least USD 1.47 billion, surpassing the previous record of USD 1.35 billion set during the 2024 election cycle, which also included the presidential race. According to Al Jazeera, OpenSecrets found that conservative groups outspent liberal groups by approximately USD 360 million in outside spending, while Democratic candidates were expected to outspend their Republican counterparts by around USD 800 million.
Political action committees, or PACs, are organisations that raise and spend money to support or oppose candidates for public office. Leadership PACs, in particular, allow elected officials and lawmakers to support other candidates and political organisations independently of their own campaign committees. (ANI)

New Zealand election early count shows tight race but National Party ahead in early projections

Reuters

07 November, 2026 01:00 pm IST

By Lucy Craymer and Alasdair Pal
WELLINGTON, Nov 7 (Reuters) – New Zealand’s ruling centre-right National Party and main opposition Labour were running neck and neck as counting began in the nationwide general election, but early projections showed the incumbent coalition would win enough seats to retain power. 

Results from the Electoral Commission show that with 14.4% of the results counted, the National Party has 30.90% of the party vote, with the centre-left Labour on 28.39% of the vote.

A seat projection from New Zealand’s Electoral Commission showed the current three-party ruling coalition led by National was heading toward remaining in control after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter disillusionment with the two biggest contenders.  

Show Full Article

“I think the (National Party) are a bit higher than we expected in complete honesty with you,” Labour lawmaker Kieran McNulty said in an interview with public broadcaster TVNZ.

“We’re not reading too much into it because it’s a relatively low level of votes that have been declared.”

Left-leaning parties including Labour are aiming to make the National Party coalition the first one-term government in nearly 50 years. 

GOVERNMENT COULD TAKE WEEKS

While the Electoral Commission expects to report preliminary results from 50% of voting places by 10 p.m. (0900 GMT), there may be no new government until after official results are released on November 27 and coalition negotiations are concluded.

New Zealand’s electoral system makes coalitions the norm, and the tightness of this year’s race means one or more of the country’s smaller parties will almost certainly participate in a governing coalition.

The country switched to a mixed member proportional system in 1996, which means people vote for both the party and a local constituency candidate.

There are 71 constituency seats and at least 49 party seats and a party or coalition needs a majority to form a government.

Special votes, which include those from overseas voters or people outside their electorate, will not be included in the vote count until November 27. Historically, special votes have favoured the left, with parties on the right losing support following the count.

New Zealand has emerged only slowly from a prolonged economic downturn, with growth subdued, household budgets strained and unemployment rising to 5.7% in the third quarter, its highest level in 11 years.

(Reporting by Alasdair Pal and Lucy Craymer in Wellington; Editing by Saad Sayeed)

items.title: カタール、米イラン仲介継続　「大きな進展」と首相
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［７日　ロイター］ - カタールのムハンマド首相は、地域情勢が制御不能に陥るのを防ぐため、米国とイランの仲介を続けていると述べた。衛星テレビ局アルジャジーラが７日報じた。

ムハンマド氏は、米政権は中間選挙後も解決策を見いだす意欲を維持しており、合意を目指す姿勢に変わりがないことを示していると述べた。

また、これまでに大きな進展があったとし、解決に向けた合意に達することができるとの自信を示した。「完璧な合意に達するまで待つわけにはいかない。良い合意に達することを望んでいる」と語った。

一方、イランの準国営タスニム通信は７日、初期段階の情報によるとケシム島にミサイル２発が着弾したもようだと報じた。被害の有無について公式情報はないとしている。米国は現時点で攻撃について発表していない。

トランプ米大統領は３日の中間選挙に先立つ数週間、イランへの攻撃を見合わせていたが、域内諸国は米国が選挙後に攻撃を再開する可能性があると見込んでいた。イランは、新たな攻撃を受ければ近隣諸国にある米国とイスラエルの標的を攻撃して報復すると繰り返し表明している。

items.title: 英メーガン妃の父親逮捕、子どもの性的虐待画像所持の疑い
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ワシントン　６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ワシントン　６日　ロイター］ - 英国のヘンリー王子の妻メーガン妃の父親トーマス・マークル容疑者（８２）が６日、子どもの性的虐待画像を所持した疑いで逮捕、訴追された。画像はカリフォルニア州の貸倉庫から見つかり、裸の未成年の少女と容疑者が一緒に写った写真も含まれている。

パテル米連邦捜査局（ＦＢＩ）長官によると、容疑者はフロリダ州で連邦捜査官に身柄を拘束された。英紙デーリー・メールによると、容疑者は同州の介護施設に入所しており、車椅子を使用しているという。

パテル氏は声明で「罪のない子どもたちを標的にし、犯罪行為によってその純真さを奪おうとした疑いがある」と説明した。司法省によると、有罪となれば最高で禁錮２０年の刑が科される可能性がある。 

容疑者は、フロリダ州タンパで連邦治安判事の前に初出廷した。ロサンゼルスの連邦検察当局の声明によると、判事は自宅拘禁と電子監視に従うことを条件に、裁判を待つ間の釈放を命じた。 

声明によると、罪状認否はまだ行われておらず、数週間先になる見通し。

英王室とメーガン妃の広報担当者は、コメントの要請に応じなかった。

items.title: India in Final-Stage Talks to Expand Missile Sale to Philippines, Sources Say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: India is in final-stage talks to expand its sale of supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters, as New Delhi nears completion of deliveries under a 2022 deal. The Philippines is expected to buy about five …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
India is in final-stage talks to expand its sale of supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters, as New Delhi nears completion of deliveries under a 2022 deal.

The Philippines is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems, nearly 60 missiles in total, in a deal potentially worth $700 million to $800 million, two of the Indian sources said.

“Manila has shown interest again to procure about 5 systems of the BrahMos, and they now view India as a very reliable partner,” one Indian source said.

New Delhi’s latest likely deal with the Philippines, which is modernizing its military and strengthening coastal defenses as tensions rise in the disputed South China Sea, is much higher than the last $375 million order of BrahMos for naval use.

BrahMos, developed jointly by India and Russia, is among the world’s fastest cruise missiles and can be launched from land, sea and air platforms.

Arsenio Andolong, Philippines defense ministry spokesperson, told Reuters that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had expressed his desire to acquire additional BrahMos missiles. Andolong did not offer more details.

Speaking virtually at the Delhi Defense Dialogue on Wednesday, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said the Philippines hoped to secure more BrahMos units and had shared a wish list with Indian authorities to tailor the system to the Philippine environment.

Reuters is the first to report the size and value of the deal.

The additional purchase comes at a time when Manila is building its military strength as tension escalates with Beijing over overlapping claims in the South China Sea, where the two countries have clashed in recent years.

India’s defence and foreign ministries, as well as missile maker BrahMos Aerospace, did not respond to requests for comment.

Interest in the BrahMos system has increased since last year’s four-day conflict between India and Pakistan, when India used the weapons system for the first time in battle.

In July, Delhi announced the supply of BrahMos missiles to Indonesia and has also signed a deal with Vietnam. It is in talks on the system with a number of other countries including UAE , Thailand, South Africa and Brazil.

India’s defense exports for the fiscal year to March reached 384.24 billion rupees ($4.11 billion), a jump of more than 62% from the same period the year before, government data showed.
